source: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
quote: Diagnostic criteria: all three of the following must be present • capillary blood glucose above 11 mmol/L

source: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
quote: Diagnostic criteria: all three of the following must be present • capillary ketones above 3 mmol/L or urine ketones ++ or more

source: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
quote: Diagnostic criteria: all three of the following must be present • venous pH less than 7.3 and/or bicarbonate less than 15 mmol/L

source: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
quote: Diagnostic criteria: all three of the following must be present • venous pH less than 7.3 and/or bicarbonate less than 15 mmol/L

source: Human Soluble Insulin
quote: 0.1unit/kg/hr based on estimate of weight 50 units human soluble insulin (Actrapid® or Humulin S®) made up to 50ml with 0.9% sodium chloride solution.

source: More cautious fluid replacement in young people aged 18-25 years, elderly, pregnant, heart or renal failure
quote: More cautious fluid replacement in young people aged 18-25 years, elderly, pregnant, heart or renal failure. (Consider HDU and/or central line)

source: Add 10% dextrose if glucose falls below 14 mmol/L
quote: Add 10% dextrose 125ml/hr if blood glucose falls below 14 mmol/L

source: Arrange follow up with specialist team
quote: Arrange follow up with specialist team

source: Assess for complications of treatment such as fluid overload and cerebral oedema
quote: Assess for complications of treatment, e.g. fluid overload, cerebral oedema

source: Check for fluid overload
quote: Check for fluid overload

source: Check venous pH, bicarbonate, potassium, capillary ketones and glucose at 12 hours
quote: At 12 hours check venous pH, bicarbonate, potassium, capillary ketones and glucose

source: Check venous pH, bicarbonate, potassium, capillary ketones and glucose at 6 hours
quote: At 6 hours check venous pH, bicarbonate, potassium, capillary ketones and glucose

source: Consider reducing insulin infusion rate to 0.05 units/kg/hour when glucose falls below 14 mmol/L
quote: Consider reducing the rate of intravenous insulin infusion to 0.05 units/ kg/hour when glucose falls below 14 mmol/L

source: Continue IV fluid replacement and avoid hypoglycaemia
quote: Continue IV fluid replacement if not eating and drinking

source: Continue IV fluid via infusion pump at reduced rate
quote: Continue IV fluid via infusion pump at reduced rate o 0.9% sodium chloride 1L with KCl over 4 hours o 0.9% sodium chloride with KCl over 6 hours

source: Convert to subcutaneous insulin when biochemically stable and patient is ready to eat
quote: Convert to subcutaneous regime when biochemically stable (capillary ketones less than 0.6 mmol/L AND pH over 7.3) and the patient is ready and able to eat

source: Define resolution of DKA as ketones <0.6 mmol/L and venous pH >7.3
quote: Resolution is defined as ketones <0.6 mmol/L, venous pH>7.3

source: Define resolution of DKA at ketones <0.6 mmol/L and venous pH >7.3
quote: Resolution of DKA is defined at ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND venous pH >7.3 (do not use bicarbonate as a marker at this stage)

source: Do not discontinue intravenous insulin until 30 minutes after subcutaneous short acting insulin has been given
quote: Do not discontinue intravenous insulin infusion until 30 minutes after subcutaneous short acting insulin has been given

source: Ensure referral to diabetes team has been made
quote: Ensure a referral has been made to the diabetes team

source: Ensure specialist team review prior to discharge for newly diagnosed patients
quote: If the patient is newly diagnosed it is essential they are seen by a member of the specialist team prior to discharge

source: Manage conversion to subcutaneous insulin by the Specialist Diabetes Team
quote: Conversion to subcutaneous insulin should be managed by the Specialist Diabetes Team.

source: Reassess cardiovascular status at 12 hours; further fluid may be required
quote: Reassess cardiovascular status at 12 hours; further fluid may be required

source: Reassess patient and monitor vital signs
quote: Re-assess patient, monitor vital signs

source: Review biochemical and metabolic parameters
quote: Review biochemical and metabolic parameters

source: Review fluid and insulin infusion if DKA not resolved
quote: If DKA not resolved review fluid Box 4 Action 1 and insulin infusion Box 3 Action 3

source: Review insulin infusion if DKA not resolved
quote: If DKA not resolved review insulin infusion (see BOX 3 Action 3)

source: Seek senior advice if patient not improving by criteria in Box 3
quote: If patient not improving by criteria in Box 3, seek senior advice

source: Transfer to subcutaneous insulin when eating and drinking normally and biochemistry is normal
quote: Transfer to subcutaneous insulin if the person is eating and drinking normally and biochemistry is normal

source: Treat precipitating factors as necessary
quote: Continue to treat precipitating factors

source: Use local guidelines if Specialist Diabetes Team is not available
quote: If the team is not available use local guidelines.
